what: Wrecks added to the main dive draw (Diving What the draw is) where wrecks are a recognised draw in dive-guide sources. A 0-10 Wreck diving rating column was NOT built: free map data misses wartime wrecks (Palau shows 2) and counts differ by source.

egypt.evidence: Egyptian Red Sea wrecks named across dive publications: SS Thistlegorm, Rosalie Moller, Carnatic, Chrisoula K, Giannis D, Kimon M, Kingston, Dunraven and Salem Express.

palau.evidence: More than 30 Japanese WWII wrecks (Fish n Fins) or 36 vessels plus aircraft (X-Ray Magazine); a ScubaDiving list names ten: Iro Maru, Chuyo Maru, Teshio Maru, Gozan, Ryuku Maru, Helmet Wreck, Bichu Maru, Amatsu Maru and others.

palawan.evidence: Coron Bay: about ten Japanese ships sunk on 24 Sep 1944 are dive sites (Akitsushima, Irako, Okikawa Maru, Kogyo Maru, Olympia Maru, Kyokuzan Maru, Morazan, Terukaze Maru and gunboats).

jordan.evidence: Aqaba: PADI lists 7 wreck dives among 18 sites (Cedar Pride, a Lockheed Tristar, the Underwater Military Museum of 19-21 vehicles, a C-130 and others); the Aqaba tourism booklet lists more.

notAdded.gbr: SS Yongala is a famous single wreck; the reef remains the draw.
notAdded.papua-new-guinea: Already recorded as reef and wrecks.
